senses.gloss:
Bhūsūkta
(‘hymn concerning मोथेर् Earth’)
------------------------------------------
It is the special characteristic of the ancient Hindu sages to see the hand of the divine—nay, the divinity itself—in every object of च्रेअतिओन्. Bhū or the earth being our basic abode that supports and sustains us, is naturally looked upon as a goddess, the मोथेर् Divine, a consort of the Supreme Lord Himself.
According to the वेदस् ‘Śrīdevī (Lakṣmī) and भूदेवी (Earth) are the spouses of Lord विष्णु (Puruṣasūkta 24; Taittirīya Saṁhitā 1.5.3.12).
There are two Bhūsūktas as available now: Atharvaveda Saṁhitā 12.1; Taittirīya Saṁhitā 1.5.3.
It is the latter सूक्त that is more well-known. The first six verses are from the Saṁhitā. The rest (12 verses) are considered खिल (addenda), but are also regularly chanted.
A brief summary of the सूक्त may now be given:
Bhūdevī pervades all the three regions (earth, हेअवेन् and sky). She affords an opportunity to the sāttvik jīvās to realise God.
By circumambulating her, सूर्य (the Sun-god) attained divinity.
It is through her grace that the वेदस् have taken refuge in him (the Sun-god).
It is again through her grace that the Sun-god has become the life-force (prāṇa) of this world of beings.
O अग्नि! Getting angry with you I forsook you! By your grace may I be able to make you burn more brilliantly!
The anger of the Lord was absorbed by भूदेवी.
She is the repository of all the gems. May she bless me with the power of all sense-organs and grant me the light of ब्रह्मन्.
She is the support or abode of (God) the Truth. She produces the best of things. She is the support of all the living beings.
The sea is her garment. The mountains are her breasts.
She is the consort of विष्णु in his इन्चर्नतिओन् as यज्ञवराह (the Boar). She is the ground for the performance of yajñas or sacrifices. She supports the river (Gaṅgā) that dropped on her from हेअवेन्.
She has the air for her breath and the ocean for her bed. She is specially gracious to the spiritually blind persons.
I bow down to भूदेवी who is also known as Mādhavī, dear to Mādhava (Viṣṇu) as his wife and the dear co-wife of लक्ष्मी.
I meditate upon भूदेवी who is armed with the bow, for attaining all that I want. May she inspire us for the same!
We offer oblations unto भूदेवी who is the consort of विष्णु, who is free from old age and who is sitting, facing her Lord.
Viṣṇu of great fame, measured the earth, the हेअवेन् and the intervening space in three steps. भूदेवी, the presiding deity of the star Śravaṇa, takes refuge in him in order to grant name and fame to her dependents.
May दूर्वा (the panic grass), which represents the divine spirit, which is superior to a thousand purifying agencies, which has hundreds of nodes and sprouts and which destroys the effects of evil द्रेअम्स्, remove all my impurities.
O भूदेवी, who is traversed by a horse, a chariot and विष्णु, I shall keep thee on my head! Protect me at every step!
O भूदेवी! You are the giver of happiness like the milch-cow. You sustain life and support all living beings. You yourself were raised by कृष्ण in his इन्चर्नतिओन् as the Boar (Varāha) having a hundred hands.
O excellent भूदेवी! Destroy my evil deeds and sins! Then I can live for a hundred years. मोथेर् Earth! Give me nourishment. In you all are established.
I invoke the presence here of Śrī, the goddess of prosperity, who is verily भूदेवी (or the earth) endowed with a peculiar aroma, who is hard to damage, who is ever well-nourished, who has an abundance of cattle and who is the ruler of all beings.
